title: Melanoma: histology report

brief.scenario: You are the core surgical trainee at a skin cancer MDT teaching encounter.
brief.task: Interpret a written report on a left calf melanoma excision biopsy. The examiner will ask for stage-relevant findings, treatment and nodal evaluation. No images are used.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Differentiate pathology of the primary tumour from overall clinical stage.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Equating diagnostic clear margins with completed treatment or ulceration with proven metastatic disease.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Read Breslow thickness, ulceration and biopsy margin status verbatim.

flow: Read the pathology report exactly and extract stage-relevant variables.
Explain Breslow thickness, ulceration, and what full stage cannot yet be concluded.
Discuss further local excision and sentinel-node staging via skin MDT.
Respond to a newly revealed palpable node without using routine SLNB as a shortcut.
Deliver an accurate, calm summary and follow-up plan.

grid.label: Extracts histology facts
grid.pass: Identifies 1.2 mm Breslow thickness, ulceration present, complete biopsy.
grid.high: Integrates pathology findings without making unsupported stage claims from missing data.

grid.label: Explains prognostic relevance
grid.pass: Explains Breslow depth and ulceration contribute to melanoma risk and staging.
grid.high: Distinguishes pathological tumour features from nodal/metastatic status.

grid.label: Explains initial staging
grid.fail: Declares final stage IV on biopsy alone.
grid.borderline: Mentions AJCC but claims exact overall stage without node status.
grid.pass: States the primary T category (1.2 mm, ulcerated) and that clinical node review is needed; avoids a definitive overall stage.
grid.high: Clarifies distinction between primary pathological T category and full clinical stage, with specialist MDT input.

grid.label: Wide local excision decision
grid.fail: Recommends no further surgery after diagnostic biopsy.
grid.pass: Plans MDT-directed wide local excision, taking stage and anatomical site into account.
grid.high: Explains NICE NG14 (1.5.3) margins: 1 cm for stage I, 2 cm for stage II, and why stage assessment matters.

grid.label: SLNB decision
grid.fail: Says SLNB is therapeutic lymphadenectomy mandatory for everyone.
grid.borderline: Mentions SLNB but not individualised discussion.
grid.pass: Discusses SLNB consideration for lesion >1 mm through skin MDT; explains it is staging.
grid.high: Balances prognostic information, discussion of benefits/harms and patient values.

grid.label: Assesses nodes and symptoms
grid.pass: Requests regional lymph node examination and symptom review.
grid.high: Distinguishes palpable-node workup from routine SLNB; selects imaging only when indicated.

grid.label: Communicates pathology
grid.pass: Explains confirmed melanoma and what biopsy does and does not show.
grid.high: Names uncertainties and expected specialist next steps in accessible language.

grid.label: Responds to palpable node cue
grid.fail: Proceeds directly to routine SLNB without assessing node.
grid.borderline: Records the new lump but takes no action.
grid.pass: Requests urgent skin-cancer MDT assessment and diagnostic evaluation of palpable node.
grid.high: Explains why clinically suspicious nodes change the pathway and need targeted investigation.

grid.label: Completes safe plan
grid.pass: Documents pathology, MDT referral, treatment/staging plan and safety-netting.
grid.high: Ensures explicit review ownership and tailored counselling without unverified prognosis figures.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What is important in the report?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It is only a small skin cancer and the margins are clear, so nothing much matters.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The width of the skin lesion. Ulceration is just a scratch, so I would ignore it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, definitely stage IV melanoma just because the lesion was ulcerated.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Does the patient require any further local treatment?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: No. A clear diagnostic biopsy means the whole treatment course is finished.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: No; it is never relevant when the skin margins are clear.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Only inspect the scar. The groin nodes cannot be involved if the biopsy margins were clear.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The patient asks if there is spread.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: “It has definitely spread through your body; the ulceration proves that.”

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: At review, a firm new lump is palpable in the ipsilateral groin.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That is probably unrelated. I would not ask the MDT about it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Discharge. No further surgery or node investigation, and no follow-up is necessary.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Here is a histology report after removal of a changing left calf lesion. Read the important findings.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It confirms invasive melanoma. The Breslow thickness is 1.2 mm, there is ulceration, and the biopsy margins are clear. The mitotic rate is also reported at three per square millimetre.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Why do depth and ulceration matter?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Breslow is vertical tumour thickness, not surface size. Thickness and ulceration influence risk and pathological T classification, so neither should be omitted from handover.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Can you assign the complete stage now?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I can discuss the primary tumour characteristics, but I cannot responsibly assign the overall stage from this histology alone without clinical nodal assessment and any indicated staging.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The margins are clear. Is treatment complete?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Not necessarily. A clear diagnostic biopsy is different from the therapeutic wide local excision. The specialist skin MDT should plan the definitive excision according to stage, location and NICE NG14 margin guidance.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Is sentinel lymph node biopsy relevant?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Yes, it should be discussed for this thickness through the MDT. SLNB is a staging procedure, not itself treatment of known nodal disease. I would explain potential value and harms before any decision.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What would you examine and ask now?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would examine regional groin nodes, the excision site and remaining skin, and ask about new lumps or systemic symptoms. I would not order routine imaging just because the patient has melanoma without applying staging criteria.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The patient asks “Does this mean it has spread?”

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would explain that melanoma is confirmed in the skin specimen, but this report alone does not tell us whether it has spread. We need to assess the lymph nodes and discuss further excision and staging tests.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: At review, a new firm left groin lump is palpable. What do you do?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would arrange urgent clinical assessment and targeted evaluation of this palpable regional node through the skin-cancer MDT. I would not assume the patient simply proceeds to routine sentinel-node staging.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Confirmed invasive 1.2 mm ulcerated melanoma of the left calf after diagnostic excision. Refer to skin MDT for definitive local excision, nodal assessment and SLNB discussion, with the new palpable groin node investigated urgently. I would document the findings and explain who will contact the patient next.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Interpret the histology of this excised left calf lesion: invasive melanoma, Breslow 1.2 mm, ulcerated, mitoses 3/mm², diagnostic margins clear.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The decisive findings are invasive cutaneous melanoma, 1.2 mm vertical Breslow thickness and microscopic ulceration; I would retain the mitotic rate and margin status in the report rather than conflate them with definitive treatment status.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Depth and ulceration underpin pathological tumour risk classification. Clear margins on the diagnostic sample are welcome but do not answer whether recommended therapeutic margins have been achieved.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What can you say about AJCC staging?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I can describe the primary tumour risk features, but a full stage requires the nodal and metastatic picture. I would not tell the patient “stage III” or “stage IV” without evidence; staging is reconciled through the specialist MDT.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What should follow the excision biopsy?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would refer promptly to the specialist skin MDT for planned therapeutic wide local excision. NICE NG14 section 1.5 differentiates margins by stage—typically 1 cm for stage I and 2 cm for stage II, with MDT consideration of anatomy and morbidity. I would not mechanically choose from Breslow alone without staging discussion.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Do you offer sentinel lymph node biopsy?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would discuss it with the MDT and patient because this lesion exceeds 1 mm. I would explain that SLNB provides prognostic staging information in clinically node-negative disease; it is not a guarantee of cure and does not replace assessment of a suspicious palpable node.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would inspect the scar and whole skin, palpate the ipsilateral inguinal nodes and review symptoms and relevant history. I would separate clinically suspicious nodes, which need diagnostic workup, from clinically negative nodes where SLNB might be discussed.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The patient worries about a death from melanoma in the family.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: “This report confirms melanoma, but it does not by itself establish spread. The next steps are to ensure the site is definitively treated and assess regional nodes appropriately.” I would acknowledge the family experience, offer written information and invite questions.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Curveball: a firm new 1.5 cm left groin node is palpable at review.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That changes the sequence. I would expedite specialist assessment and targeted ultrasound with needle sampling as directed by the MDT rather than treating a clinically suspicious node as a routine sentinel-node procedure. I would discuss any further staging only after establishing the nature of the node.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Close with your handover and documentation.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: “Ulcerated 1.2 mm invasive melanoma, diagnostic margins clear, regional nodal status unresolved and now a new palpable ipsilateral groin node.” I would ensure named MDT ownership, a documented investigation and definitive local-treatment plan, and balanced counselling without invented survival percentages.

failures.move: Assigning disseminated disease from ulceration alone
failures.consequence: risks major misinformation and harmful management decisions.

failures.move: Omitting specialist assessment for wide local excision

failures.consequence: risks delayed diagnosis of nodal metastatic disease.

recovery.when: Correcting the implication of a clear diagnostic margin
recovery.line: I should correct the implication of a clear diagnostic margin: the skin MDT must still decide the therapeutic excision margin and stage-specific plan.
A newly palpable regional node needs a diagnostic assessment now; it should not simply be routed into routine sentinel-node discussion.

knowledge.fact: Breslow thickness is measured tumour depth; ulceration is a separate staging feature.
NG14 advises against imaging or SLNB in stage IA melanoma.
NG14 1.4.3 considers SLNB at 0.8–1.0 mm only with specified additional risk factors; higher-risk melanomas should be discussed through specialist staging pathways.
NICE NG14 clinical excision margins are stage dependent: 1 cm for stage I (or where a 2 cm margin causes unacceptable morbidity), 2 cm for stage II.
The presence of a palpable suspicious node changes assessment: routine SLNB is not a substitute for diagnostic evaluation of clinically suspicious lymphadenopathy.
Normal diagnostic biopsy margins do not by themselves remove the need for discussion of wide local excision and MDT management.
A 1.2 mm ulcerated melanoma is pT2b (AJCC 8th edition); if sentinel node biopsy is negative it is stage II, so NICE NG14 recommends a 2 cm clinical excision margin.

recall.think: Thickness and ulceration describe primary tumour risk, not proven spread.
recall.say: “The melanoma diagnosis is confirmed; the stage is not yet fully established.”
do: Skin MDT, therapeutic excision plan, regional-node assessment and SLNB discussion.

numbers.meaning: NICE NG14 excision clinical margins: stage I
NICE NG14 excision clinical margins: stage II (context matters)

recall.trap: A clear biopsy margin is not the same as completion of definitive care.
recall.finish: Document the new-node investigation and patient contact arrangements.

sources.name: NICE. Melanoma: assessment and management (NG14).
sources.supports: Recommendations 1.4 (sentinel lymph node biopsy) and 1.5 (excision margins). Work-up of a palpable node follows skin-cancer MDT practice, not a specific NG14 recommendation.

partner.opening: Interpret a written report on a left calf melanoma excision biopsy.

reveals.finding: 1.2 mm ulcerated invasive melanoma of left calf, mitoses 3/mm², diagnostic margins clear. No diagnostic image.
regional nodes are not yet assessed; do not disclose any palpable node until G8.

reveals.trigger: If asked about distant symptoms before the curveball
reveals.finding: say none is reported; do not volunteer the new groin node.

push.question: Ask the candidate what Breslow thickness and ulceration mean and whether full AJCC stage can be assigned.
Ask about definitive local excision, sentinel-node discussion and relevant clinical assessment.
At G7, use a patient worry about spread or family melanoma history; candidate responds as they would to the patient.

curveballs.prompt: At G8 reveal a new firm 1.5 cm left groin node, prompting a change from clinically node-negative staging discussion to targeted workup.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Requests urgent skin-cancer MDT assessment and diagnostic evaluation of palpable node.
